routes.name: otp-send
routes.description: Request a phone OTP. Public per AGENT-BRIEF explicit allowlist.

routes.name: otp-verify
routes.description: Verify a phone OTP and mint tokens. Public per AGENT-BRIEF explicit allowlist; also phone+IP limited because this is the OTP brute-force surface.

routes.name: auth-register-email
routes.description: Register a patient with email and password. Public; user-service rate-limits per email and per IP. Doctors are not created here.

routes.name: auth-login-email
routes.description: Email and password login for patients and doctors. Public; the password is the credential. User-service rate-limits per email.

routes.name: auth-oauth-google
routes.description: Google ID-token login. Public; user-service verifies the token with Google and mints the platform JWT.

routes.name: auth-refresh
routes.description: Rotate a refresh token into a new access token. PUBLIC by necessity: the caller's access token has expired, which is the entire reason it is calling. The refresh token itself is the credential, and user-service verifies it, detects reuse and refuses suspended accounts. Rate-limited harder than a normal read because it is a credential-presentation endpoint. Its absence from this table meant every session died 15 minutes after login with no way to renew.

routes.name: auth-logout
routes.description: Revoke the presented refresh token. Public for the same reason as refresh: a client logging out after its access token expired must still be able to kill the session. Idempotent upstream.

routes.name: auth-logout-all
routes.description: Revoke every session for the caller. Requires a live access token because it acts on the whole account, not one presented token.

routes.name: user-me-get
routes.description: Current user profile.

routes.name: user-me-put
routes.description: Update current user profile.

routes.name: user-me-password
routes.description: Set or change the caller's password so they can use email login after an OTP or Google session.

routes.name: user-me-photo-put
routes.description: Upload or replace the caller's profile photograph (JPEG/PNG/WebP, max 2 MB).

routes.name: user-me-photo-get
routes.description: Download the caller's profile photograph bytes.

routes.name: user-me-photo-delete
routes.description: Remove the caller's profile photograph.

routes.name: user-me-delete
routes.description: Request PDPA account deletion. Soft-deletes now and schedules erasure after the support grace window.

routes.name: user-family-list
routes.description: List the caller's family member profiles.

routes.name: user-family-post
routes.description: Add a family member profile. NOTE the /me/ segment: user-service registers this subtree under /users/me/family, and this entry previously omitted it, so every call 404'd at the upstream.

routes.name: user-family-put
routes.description: Update a family member profile.

routes.name: user-family-delete
routes.description: Remove a family member profile.

routes.name: doctor-apply
routes.description: Public doctor application before OTP. No account is created until admin approval and OTP.

routes.name: doctor-application-eligibility
routes.description: Whether a phone may complete doctor-portal OTP (approved application or already activated).

routes.name: doctor-apply-documents
routes.description: Upload a signature, seal, or SLMC certificate onto a pending public application. No account exists yet; the application id is the capability.

routes.name: doctor-register
routes.description: Begin doctor onboarding. Any authenticated user; doctor-service enforces the rest.

routes.name: doctor-search
routes.description: Search approved doctors. Public per AGENT-BRIEF explicit allowlist.

routes.name: doctor-me-get
routes.description: The calling doctor's own profile, including verification status. Static /me beats the /{doctorID} pattern in chi's tree, so this does not shadow doctor-detail.

routes.name: doctor-me-put
routes.description: Edit the calling doctor's profile (fee, specialty, languages, bio, qualifications). Optimistic-locked on version upstream.

routes.name: doctor-availability-get
routes.description: Read the calling doctor's declared weekly working hours.

routes.name: doctor-availability-put
routes.description: Declare weekly working hours. Doctor role only.

routes.name: doctor-schedule-settings-get
routes.description: Read back the slot-shape settings saved by the availability editor (slot duration, buffer, daily cap, timezone). It is a separate endpoint from GET /doctors/me/availability because that one responds with a bare working-hours array and widening it to an object would break the doctor app's parser; without this the settings would be write-only, and the editor would show defaults on a second device with no way to know they are wrong.

routes.name: doctor-documents-post
routes.description: Attach a credential document (SLMC certificate, NIC, degree certificate, photo) to the calling doctor's application. The body carries only the object key -- bytes go straight to object storage -- so this is a write, not an upload.

routes.name: doctor-detail
routes.description: Public doctor profile. Public per AGENT-BRIEF explicit allowlist.

routes.name: doctor-reviews-get
routes.description: Published, moderated patient reviews for a doctor. Public for the same reason as doctor search and doctor detail, which it is part of: a patient chooses a doctor by rating before creating an account, and doctor-service serves this route under OptionalAuth. Carries no PHI -- rating, comment and publication state only.

routes.name: doctor-reviews-post
routes.description: Leave a review for a completed appointment. doctor-service enforces one review per appointment and that the caller actually attended it.

routes.name: doctor-slots-get
routes.description: Available slots for a doctor on a date. Owned by scheduling-service, not doctor-service: chi resolves this more specific pattern ahead of doctor-service's /{doctorID}.

routes.name: appointments-post
routes.description: Book a slot. Patient role only.

routes.name: appointments-list
routes.description: The caller's appointments. One endpoint serves both sides: scheduling-service scopes the query by the principal's role, so a doctor gets their schedule and a patient gets their bookings. This is what the doctor app's dashboard calls -- there is no /doctors/me/appointments in doctor-service, and the entry that used to claim there was routed every call to a 404.

routes.name: appointment-detail
routes.description: One appointment. scheduling-service authorises that the caller is a party to it.

routes.name: appointments-cancel
routes.description: Cancel an appointment. Either party may; scheduling-service applies the refund policy.

routes.name: appointment-complete
routes.description: Close out a consultation as completed. Doctor only -- scheduling-service refuses a patient outright, and this role gate is the same rule stated at the edge.

routes.name: appointment-no-show
routes.description: Mark a patient no-show. Doctor only: a patient must not be able to declare their own no-show, nor close out a consultation to dodge one.

routes.name: appointment-reschedule-create
routes.description: Doctor proposes a new time for a confirmed booking. scheduling-service holds the instant and notifies admin and the patient.

routes.name: appointment-reschedule-list
routes.description: Reschedule requests for one appointment. scheduling-service scopes to a party of the booking.

routes.name: reschedule-accept
routes.description: Patient of that booking, or an administrator, accepts the move. Same appointment id and payment; no cancel event.

routes.name: reschedule-decline
routes.description: Patient of that booking, or an administrator, declines. Original booking is cancelled with a full refund.

routes.name: waitlist-post
routes.description: Join a doctor's waitlist. Patient role only.

routes.name: consultation-join
routes.description: Join a consultation and mint a LiveKit token. The path id here is the APPOINTMENT id -- join, ready-for-next and early-join are keyed that way, and the join response returns consultation_id for every call below. The path parameter is named {consultationID} to match its siblings because chi permits only one parameter name per position in its tree; the value is an appointment id.

routes.name: consultation-get
routes.description: Consultation state and participants. Keyed by consultation id, from the join response.

routes.name: consultation-admit
routes.description: Doctor admits a waiting patient. Keyed by consultation id.

routes.name: consultation-end
routes.description: End the call. Either party may. Keyed by consultation id.

routes.name: consultation-consent
routes.description: Record a telemedicine or recording consent decision. This is the endpoint that GATES RECORDING: egress starts only once both parties have granted. It was absent from this table, so recording consent could not be given through the gateway at all.

routes.name: consultation-waiting-room
routes.description: Queue position and estimated wait for a waiting patient. Keyed by consultation id.

routes.name: consultation-quality
routes.description: Report a connection-quality sample and learn whether to downgrade video. Called repeatedly during a call on a bad 3G link, so it is rate-limited generously and timed as a read.

routes.name: consultation-ready-for-next
routes.description: Doctor finished early: ping only the immediate next patient asking if they can join now. Does not rewrite later slots. Uses the doctor's latest ended consult as the previous visit.

routes.name: consultation-ready-for-next-after
routes.description: Same as consultation-ready-for-next, keyed by the ended visit's APPOINTMENT id (join-style path param named {consultationID}).

routes.name: consultation-early-join-get
routes.description: Patient view of a pending join-now offer. Path id is the APPOINTMENT id.

routes.name: consultation-early-join-accept
routes.description: Patient agrees to join a few minutes early. Does not move scheduled_at; they join through the existing waiting room.

routes.name: consultation-early-join-decline
routes.description: Patient keeps the original booked time. No refund, no slot rewrite.

routes.name: payment-intent-post
routes.description: Create a payment intent for an appointment.

routes.name: payments-list
routes.description: The caller's payments. payment-service scopes by principal.

routes.name: payment-get
routes.description: Payment status.

routes.name: payment-order-get
routes.description: The server's price breakdown for a booking. The payment screen renders this instead of subtracting a discount itself: a total computed on the handset is a total an attacker controls.

routes.name: payment-promo-apply
routes.description: Reserve a promo code against the caller's pending payment. Moderate rate limit, not generous: this is the endpoint someone would use to guess codes.

routes.name: payment-promo-remove
routes.description: Take the promo code back off a booking and return it to its pool.

routes.name: payment-promo-codes-get
routes.description: List promotions. Role-gated at the edge as well as in payment-service, so a patient token is refused before it reaches an upstream. Not auth mode 'admin': promo management lives under /payments and is reached by finance staff, not only from the admin-web IP allowlist.

routes.name: payment-promo-codes-post
routes.description: Issue a promotion. A promo code is a standing instruction to give money away, so it is finance's decision.

routes.name: payment-promo-codes-delete
routes.description: Withdraw a promotion. Reservations already held are left alone.

routes.name: payment-dialog-request-pin
routes.description: Send a carrier-billing PIN by SMS. Moderate, not generous: every call costs an SMS and reaches Dialog.

routes.name: payment-dialog-confirm
routes.description: Enter the carrier-billing PIN. The attempt allowance in payment-service is the real brute-force defence; this limit is the outer one.

routes.name: payment-confirm-pin
routes.description: Payment-keyed twin of /payments/dialog/confirm, for support tooling and any client that already holds the payment id. payment-service registers it and it was not routed at all.

routes.name: payment-refund-post
routes.description: Refund a payment. payment-service applies the cancellation policy and refuses a patient asserting who cancelled. Registered and previously unrouted.

routes.name: payment-invoice-get
routes.description: Invoice PDF. Upload timeout class because it renders a document, not because it uploads one.

routes.name: payment-ledger-get
routes.description: The double-entry legs behind one payment. Finance's view of the money, not the patient's receipt.

routes.name: payment-methods-get
routes.description: The caller's saved cards. Display metadata only: the provider token never leaves payment-service.

routes.name: payment-methods-post
routes.description: Record the card a completed provider SetupIntent produced.

routes.name: payment-methods-setup-intent
routes.description: Begin saving a card. Returns the provider client secret the SDK sheet confirms against; the card number goes handset-to-provider and never transits this gateway.

routes.name: payment-method-delete
routes.description: Delete a saved card. Detaches the token at the rail first.

routes.name: payment-method-default-put
routes.description: Make a saved card the default.

routes.name: payouts-list
routes.description: Payouts visible to the caller. No role gate: payment-service scopes by the principal's doctor_id and returns an empty list -- not a 403 -- to a caller with none, which is what keeps the endpoint from leaking that payouts exist. Backs the doctor app's earnings screen.

routes.name: payouts-run
routes.description: Trigger a payout batch: the single highest-value money mutation on the platform. Auth mode 'admin', not merely role-gated. The previous note here claimed the admin IP allowlist only wraps /api/v1/admin/* -- it does not: router.go's composeMiddleware applies IPAllowlist, restrictOrigin and RequireTokenIssuer by AUTH MODE, per rule, and the URL prefix is a naming convention. Leaving this route on auth mode 'authenticated' therefore ran the platform's payout trigger with no IP allowlist, no admin-origin rejection and no issuer binding, all of which every read-only /admin/analytics route already had. The prefix convention is preserved by an explicit, named exception in routes_test.go.

routes.name: webhook-stripe
routes.description: Stripe webhook. Public per AGENT-BRIEF explicit allowlist; payment-service verifies the signature.

routes.name: webhook-payhere
routes.description: PayHere webhook. Public per AGENT-BRIEF explicit allowlist; payment-service verifies the signature.

routes.name: webhook-dialog
routes.description: Dialog Genie webhook. Public per AGENT-BRIEF explicit allowlist; payment-service verifies the signature.

routes.name: webhook-livekit
routes.description: LiveKit room/egress webhook. Public per AGENT-BRIEF explicit allowlist; consultation-service verifies the signature.

routes.name: notifications-get
routes.description: In-app notification list.

routes.name: notification-read-put
routes.description: Mark one notification read. PUT, not POST: notification-service registers it as PUT.

routes.name: notification-preferences-get
routes.description: Read channel and quiet-hours preferences. Static 'preferences' beats the /{notificationID} pattern in chi's tree.

routes.name: notification-preferences-put
routes.description: Update channel and quiet-hours preferences. PUT, not POST: this entry previously declared POST, which notification-service does not register, so every preference save 405'd.

routes.name: notification-read-all-put
routes.description: Clear the whole unread badge. Static 'read-all' beats the /{notificationID} pattern in chi's tree.

routes.name: notification-devices-post
routes.description: Register or refresh an FCM device token. notification-service has registered this since day one and it was never routed, so push registration was unreachable through the only ingress the mobile apps have -- which is why the patient app invented POST /users/me/push-token.

routes.name: notification-device-delete
routes.description: Invalidate a device token on sign-out. Also registered and never routed.

routes.name: prescriptions-post
routes.description: Issue an e-prescription. Doctor role only.

routes.name: prescriptions-by-appointment-get
routes.description: Look up the prescription issued for an appointment (?appointment_id=). Patient, treating doctor, or active share.

routes.name: prescription-get
routes.description: One prescription, for a party to it. Static /verify lives at /api/v1/verify/prescriptions, so it does not collide with this parameter.

routes.name: prescription-pdf-get
routes.description: Rendered prescription PDF. Upload timeout class because record-service renders the document on demand.

routes.name: prescription-verify-get
routes.description: Pharmacist prescription verification by QR. Public per AGENT-BRIEF explicit allowlist. The path is /verify/prescriptions/{id}, which is where record-service mounts it -- this entry previously declared /prescriptions/verify/{id}, a path no service registers, so every pharmacist scan 404'd.

routes.name: records-list
routes.description: The caller's medical record vault. record-service scopes by principal and logs the access.

routes.name: records-upload-post
routes.description: Upload a medical record. Static 'upload' beats the /{recordID} pattern in chi's tree.

routes.name: record-get
routes.description: One record's metadata.

routes.name: records-delete
routes.description: Soft-delete a vault document. Owning patient only.

routes.name: records-download-get
routes.description: Download a medical record.

routes.name: drugs-search
routes.description: Drug reference search, backing the prescription builder's autocomplete. Authenticated with no role gate, matching record-service's own registration: this is clinical reference data, not patient data.

routes.name: admin-doctors-pending
routes.description: Doctor verification queue. Admin auth mode: role check plus the IP allowlist.

routes.name: admin-doctors-verify
routes.description: Approve or reject a doctor. Admin auth mode.

routes.name: admin-analytics-revenue
routes.description: Revenue analytics. Admin auth mode.

routes.name: admin-users-create
routes.description: Create an admin account, provisioning its Keycloak login. Super_admin only, enforced by admin-service. Write timeout: this call fans out to the identity provider.

routes.name: doctor-availability-admin-read
routes.description: Read a doctor's weekly working hours as staff. auth:admin, so the IP allowlist and admin origin restriction apply -- the same protections /api/v1/admin/* carries.

routes.name: doctor-availability-admin-write
routes.description: Set a doctor's weekly working hours as staff. Doctors phone their hours in; an administrator enters them. Regenerates slots downstream, hence the write timeout.

routes.name: doctor-schedule-settings-admin-read
routes.description: Read a doctor's slot shape (duration, buffer, daily cap). Staff need it to see what they are about to overwrite.

routes.name: doctor-application-admin-get
routes.description: Public-apply profile fields for credential review. Bank account number is never returned.

routes.name: doctor-application-admin-document
routes.description: Raw signature, seal, or SLMC certificate uploaded with a public apply.

routes.name: admin-reschedule-requests-list
routes.description: Pending doctor-requested reschedules. Named ahead of admin-catchall so the request reaches scheduling-service, which owns the rows.

routes.name: admin-reschedule-accept
routes.description: Administrator accepts a pending reschedule after talking to the patient. Moves the same paid appointment.

routes.name: admin-reschedule-decline
routes.description: Administrator declines a pending reschedule. Cancels the original booking with a full refund.

routes.name: admin-catchall
routes.description: Everything else under the admin prefix. Named routes above exist for documentation and per-route timeouts; this guarantees no admin path can be reached without the IP allowlist by being absent from the table.

routes.name: clinical-notes-list
routes.description: A doctor's own clinical notes, paginated. record-service scopes to the caller.

routes.name: clinical-notes-save
routes.description: SOAP autosave. This route's absence was a CRITICAL client finding: the doctor app queued every note for an endpoint that 404'd, the 404 was classified non-retryable so entries were kept, and a doctor's entire clinical-note history accumulated unencrypted on the handset forever.

routes.name: clinical-notes-get
routes.description: Read one clinical note. Authorised and access-logged by record-service.

routes.name: clinical-notes-finalise
routes.description: Sign a clinical note. Immutable thereafter except by amendment.

routes.name: clinical-notes-amend
routes.description: Amend a finalised note; writes an append-only revision rather than overwriting.

routes.name: clinical-notes-revisions
routes.description: The amendment trail for a note.

routes.name: icd10-search
routes.description: ICD-10 reference search. A published classification, no patient data, so authenticated but not role-gated -- same treatment as /drugs.

routes.name: test-status
routes.description: the test surface's own capability report

routes.name: test-outbox-list
routes.description: captured OTP and email messages, newest first

routes.name: test-outbox-latest
routes.description: the most recent captured message for one recipient

routes.name: test-outbox-clear
routes.description: drop everything captured so far

routes.name: test-room-create
routes.description: mint a signalling room token for a browser

routes.name: test-room-get
routes.description: local peer count for a signalling room

routes.name: test-room-close
routes.description: evict both peers from a signalling room

routes.name: test-ice-servers
routes.description: the STUN/TURN configuration handed to browsers
